content:
Dating reality shows have always been a popular genre, but Apple TV+ has never ventured into it. Although its newly announced series "The Last Person on Earth" is positioned as a "documentary series" rather than a "reality show," it is still the platform's first dating programme.

"The Last Person on Earth" features renowned couples therapist Esther Perel and is described as an "innovative experiment"

Esther Perel is a well-known couples therapist and New York Times bestselling author, specialising in interpersonal relationships.

Perel is also the central figure in Apple TV+'s newly announced 8-episode dating documentary series "The Last Person on Earth".

According to the press release: "In the series, partners who appear to be poles apart will be carefully matched by Perel and a team of matching experts and therapists, before travelling together to one of the most romantic and remote places on earth."

It sounds very much like a reality show, but it avoids the baggage that comes with the reality show brand. I suspect Apple has taken an "upgrade" approach for its dating series, hence the "documentary series" label.

Here's Perel introducing the show's content in person:

The series has not yet set a premiere date and is expected to debut within 2027.

Incidentally, Apple also announced yesterday that it will adapt the latest romance novel from bestselling author Rebecca Yarros into a TV series. The streaming platform clearly hopes to break beyond its current core genres of sci-fi, comedy and thriller, and venture into new territory.

Apple TV+ costs US$12.99 per month, and discounts are also available through an Apple One bundle subscription.
